case_analysis.thread_summary: This is an internal/lab-coordination thread (June 13-25, 2025) for an RF 2-item logo test of a Ricoh Imaging DSC (digital camera) at the ABTS test lab (Leo Chou), arranged by Allion's Mochizuki. After testing, the lab observed the measured output power didn't match LE Power Class 1 and flagged that digital cameras are typically non-Power-Class-1 by design. The customer initially confirmed 'Class 2' and revised the test plan's ICS accordingly, but the lab pushed back: 'Power Class 2' isn't a defined category in the current ICS/Test Specification (only Power Class 1 yes/no for LE, and only a Power Class 1 level for classic RF output power per the updated TCRL) - it's a Core Specification concept only. The lab requested the report be made as 'non-Class 1' instead and sent a revised Test Plan ICS image reflecting the latest definitions. Separately, a Model Name typo carried over from the test plan into the report was identified and corrected, with the lab confirming no other issues and sending the updated report; Sakai closed out the thread on Mochizuki's behalf thanking the lab for the quick turnaround.
all_questions_found: (Internal/lab) Based on the measured output power, is this digital camera's Bluetooth module LE Power Class 1, and if not, how should that be reflected in the ICS/report?
(Internal/lab) Is 'Power Class 2' a valid designation for the ICS/RF report given the current ICS and Test Specification (TCRL) only define Power Class 1 support/non-support?
(Internal/lab) Can the report's Model Name field be corrected to match the corrected Test Plan, with no other changes needed?
case_analysis.key_technical_discussion: Measured RF output power (Low/Mid/High P_average approx. -2.82 to -3.84 dBm, PPK-PAVG 0.08-0.11) indicated the DUT was not LE Power Class 1, consistent with typical low-power digital camera Bluetooth designs. The customer's first response revised the ICS to 'Class 2' and asked for a Class 2 report, but the lab clarified that 'Power Class 2' is a Bluetooth Core Specification power-level concept not present as an option in the current ICS or Test Specification/TCRL - which for LE only define 'Power Class 1: support or not support', and for classic RF output power testing per the updated TCRL only define a Power Class 1 level. The lab therefore requested the report be made as 'non-Class 1' and provided a revised Test Plan ICS image aligned to the latest definitions. A separate, unrelated Model Name typo in the report (carried over from an earlier Test Plan version) was also corrected, with the lab confirming no other issues in the report.
case_analysis.key_decision_logic: RF Power Class classification was driven by measured output power data interpreted against ICS/Test Specification/TCRL-defined categories rather than informal Core Specification terminology: since 'Power Class 2' is not a defined ICS/TCRL answer option, the lab recommended 'non-Power-Class-1' as the correct classification and supplied an updated ICS image to align the Test Plan with current definitions. Administrative corrections (Model Name) were handled separately and verified not to affect the substantive test results.
case_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Recording a device's ICS/RF report as 'Power Class 2' when that designation isn't defined in the current ICS/Test Specification/TCRL could create an inconsistent or non-conformant report and ICS that may require correction before acceptance into the qualification submission. An uncorrected Model Name typo carried from the test plan into the final report could cause a mismatch with the product registration details.
case_analysis.consulting_mistake: An earlier Test Plan version contained a Model Name typo that was carried into the initial RF test report; this required a follow-up correction cycle before the report could be finalized.
case_analysis.consulting_takeaway: When a device's measured output power doesn't match LE Power Class 1, don't simply relabel the ICS/report as 'Power Class 2' - verify whether that designation is a defined option in the current ICS and Test Specification/TCRL (it generally is not; only Power Class 1 support/non-support is defined). If not defined, classify the device as 'non-Power-Class-1' and update the Test Plan's ICS to the latest defined image. Also double-check that Model Name and other identifying fields in the Test Plan and report match the customer's confirmed product naming before finalizing.
